changed.reason: The current cell distance does not exclude off-support mass. Arbitrarily small off-support mass at arbitrarily large outcomes can preserve the listed witness cells while reversing prediction risks and gradient variances. Restricting the norm to the complete joint cell vector on the witness's fixed finite support makes the intended finite-cell topology mathematically well-defined and makes all relevant rational functionals continuous.

note: Mandatory maximality review IMPROVE: six-target whole-paper repair; no D0.5 advance.
directive: Whole-paper maximality repair, all in one scoped round. (1) Repair lem:designwise-gradient under the EXISTING assumptions: its proof currently applies early-proxy completeness to a function of (S2d,U,X) although the stated premise quantifies functions of U. Do not strengthen completeness, restrict X/S2d, or add a crux-encoding premise merely to save the claim. Re-derive identification faithfully from the frozen anchor assumptions; re-audit the canonical-gradient tangent-space argument. If the exact general claim is unreachable under those same assumptions, propose the strongest honest narrowing rather than laundering it. (2) Strengthen thm:predictive-impossibility to genuinely unequal design costs: use the existing inequality Cp/Ce < 3(16-9 epsilon^2)/[35(1-epsilon^2)] with limit 48/35 to give an explicit cap-feasible catalogue, preferably with dp more expensive, and prove divergence on an open range of cost vectors. (3) Make def:binary-region rigorous: replace the unjustified fixed 10^-6 epsilon^4 radius by explicit uniform constants or a proved existential/adaptive radius, and distinguish relative openness in the constrained regular model from ambient-simplex openness. (4) Replace or demote thm:finite-catalogue-predictive-guarantee: finite catalogue plus positive variances gives only a tautological law-specific enumerated ratio. Derive a genuinely nontrivial primitive operator/moment-envelope certificate with the necessary two-sided generalized-condition-number structure and catalogue-restricted attainment; if unavailable under maintained assumptions, state the impossibility and retain the exact finite maximum only as a diagnostic remark, not a headline theorem. (5) Preserve and state the already-proved second-order allocation rate O_P((rV,m+vbar_m)^2+B^-1). In the witness give the exact O(1) remainder for VO,dp and the leading constant for rho_pred. (6) Synchronize tldr, project_justification gap/niche/fill, and related_work: call the comparator this paper’s CLW-shaped paired-source transplant, not a workflow/guarantee asserted by Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm; clarify B excludes the separately funded full-catalogue pilot; label designwise bijectivity, bridge existence for every candidate, uniform nuisance rates, and variance-estimation rates as maintained extensions rather than Standard. Use no strengthen-to-prove move and preserve the field-level cost-aware inverse-geometry headline.

changed.from: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(\tau=\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}\) is identified, and under independent sample sizes \(n_E,n_O\) its canonical gradient decomposes into the two sample components \(\phi_{E,d}/n_E\) and \(\phi_{O,d}/n_O\), giving local variance \(V_{E,d}/n_E+V_{O,d}/n_O\).
changed.to: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\), the observed-data bridge contrast \(\theta_d(P):=\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}\) is identified.  Along every regular two-source submodel its pathwise gradient has source components \(\phi_{E,d}\) and \(\phi_{O,d}\), so independent sample sizes \(n_E,n_O\) give gradient variance \(V_{E,d}/n_E+V_{O,d}/n_O\).  The frozen assumptions do not in general imply \(\theta_d(P)=\tau\): there is a finite-support law in \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) for which \(\theta_d(P)=0\) and \(\tau=-3/25\).  Thus the displayed gradient is not a canonical gradient for the causal target \(\tau\) on the entire frozen class.
changed.reason: The frozen completeness implication is injective only for a common function of U. The outcome-bridge discrepancy generally depends on the middle proxy and covariates. The explicit finite-support counterexample satisfies every frozen premise, including both completeness conditions, bijectivity, bridge existence, and nondegenerate score variances, but has bridge contrast 0 and causal ATE -3/25. The observed bridge functional and its gradient remain identified.

changed.from: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and fixed \(0<\alpha<1\), as \(B\to\infty\) the floor-count local semiparametric efficiency bound satisfies \(B\{V_{E,d}/n_{E,B}(d,\alpha)+V_{O,d}/n_{O,B}(d,\alpha)\}=\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)+\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\), where \(0\le\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\le 2B^{-1}\{V_{E,d}c_{E,d}^2/\alpha^2+V_{O,d}c_{O,d}^2/(1-\alpha)^2\}\) once \(B\ge2\max\{c_{E,d}/\alpha,c_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\}\). Hence the floor-count bound converges to \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\). The unique minimizer and minimum of this limiting profile are \(\alpha_d^*(P)=\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}/(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})\) and \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2\).
changed.to: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and fixed \(0<\alpha<1\), as \(B\to\infty\) the floor-count variance of the designwise bridge-functional gradient satisfies \(B\{V_{E,d}/n_{E,B}(d,\alpha)+V_{O,d}/n_{O,B}(d,\alpha)\}=\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)+\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\), where \(0\le\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\le 2B^{-1}\{V_{E,d}c_{E,d}^2/\alpha^2+V_{O,d}c_{O,d}^2/(1-\alpha)^2\}\) once \(B\ge2\max\{c_{E,d}/\alpha,c_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\}\). Hence the floor-count variance converges to \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\). The unique minimizer and minimum of this limiting profile are \(\alpha_d^*(P)=\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}/(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})\) and \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2\).  Whenever the designwise bridge functional equals \(\tau\) and the displayed gradient is canonical for \(\tau\), including the binary witness subclass below, the same quantity is the budget-normalized local semiparametric efficiency bound for \(\tau\).
changed.reason: The floor and allocation algebra is valid for the designwise observed bridge-functional gradient variance. Calling it the causal semiparametric efficiency bound for every law would inherit the false causal equality in the original designwise-gradient lemma. The proposed statement retains the causal efficiency interpretation exactly on subclasses where that equality and canonicality are established, including the binary witness.

changed.from: For the explicit two-design family \(P_{\epsilon}\), every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives a law in \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\): both binary conditional-expectation matrices have nonzero determinant, both completeness conditions hold, and the displayed bridges satisfy \(\|h_d\|_{\infty}<\infty\), \(\|q_d\|_{\infty}<\infty\), and finite fourth moments for each \(d\). The two designs have equal costs \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\) and \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=4\), hence equal jointly budget-feasible sample sizes \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/7\). Therefore the cost-aware comparator reduces within this equal-cost subclass to the displayed residual-variance ordering: \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\epsilon};B)=7(1-\epsilon^2)(7/16)/[B(1-9\epsilon^2/16)]<21/(5B)=\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_{\epsilon};B)\). Thus \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), and the prespecified tie rule is immaterial on the witness path. Yet \(V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=4(1/16)(7/9)/[(15/16)^2\epsilon^2]+O(\epsilon^{-1})\), while \(V_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}\), \(V_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}\), and \(V_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}\) remain bounded and nondegenerate; consequently \(D^*(P_{\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\epsilon})\to\infty\). Moreover, every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\cap D^*(P)=\varnothing\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). Thus the cost-aware prediction-efficiency workflow of CarneiroLeeWilhelm2020 has no finite approximation-ratio analogue in this persistent-confounding bridge model.
changed.to:
For the unequal-cost binary witness, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives a law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) for which both designs identify \(\tau\) and are regular. Although \(d_{\mathrm p}\) is more expensive, with \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=6>5=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}\), it is the unique minimizer of this paper's Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped paired-source prediction objective, while \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is the unique minimizer of the causal design value. More precisely,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},\qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). The same divergence holds on the relatively open range of cap-feasible cost vectors satisfying
\[
 1<\frac{c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}}
 {c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}}<\frac{48}{35},
\]
for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\). Thus the failure is neither an equal-cost artifact nor an identification failure.

Let \(\mathcal D\) be finite and nonempty.  Suppose the costs and population variance components obey
\[
 0<\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\min\{c_{E,d},c_{O,d},V_{E,d},V_{O,d}\}
 \le
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{c_{E,d},c_{O,d},V_{E,d},V_{O,d}\}<\infty.
\]
Suppose
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\bigl\{
 |\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,
 |\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\bigr\}=O_P(r_{V,m}),
 \qquad r_{V,m}=o(1),
 \qquad \underline v_m\downarrow0,
\]
and define \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}\) by the full-catalogue pilot selector.  Then, along every joint sequence \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\),
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\left|B\left\{
 \frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}
 +\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}
 \right\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)\right|
 =O_P\!\left((r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)^2+B^{-1}\right).
\]
In particular, allocation estimation enters the profiled value only at second order.
changed.reason: The inherited phrase referring to another theorem's hypotheses is circular and does not expose the asymptotic regime. The replacement states exactly the finite-family, positivity, nondegeneracy, pilot-rate, truncation, and joint-limit conditions used by the proof.

Let \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\), and assume that \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose that for fixed \(L\), uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(1\le\ell\le L\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), and \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and \(\min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2})\). Under the full-catalogue pilot law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\) with \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\) with \(r_{\widetilde V,B}=o(1)\). For \(\widehat d_m\) and the feasible share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), form the realized counts \(N_{E,B},N_{O,B}\) and define \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) from the selected foldwise source-score second moments. Then \(B\{V_{E,\widehat d_m}/N_{E,B}+V_{O,\widehat d_m}/N_{O,B}\}-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), and
\[
 \frac{\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-(\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0})\}}
 {\widehat s_B}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
The corresponding two-sided standard-normal Wald interval has coverage tending to \(1-\eta\) for the pilot-selected bridge contrast \(\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0}\). If, in addition, \(\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}=\tau\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\), then the same studentized limit is centered at \(\tau\) and the same interval has coverage tending to \(1-\eta\) for the observational-population long-term average treatment effect.

Let \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\), assume \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), and assume that \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose that for fixed \(L\), uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(1\le\ell\le L\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), and \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and \(\min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2})\). Under the full-catalogue pilot law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\) with \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\) with \(r_{\widetilde V,B}=o(1)\). For \(\widehat d_m\) and the feasible share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), form the realized counts \(N_{E,B},N_{O,B}\) and define \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) from the selected foldwise source-score second moments. Then \(B\{V_{E,\widehat d_m}/N_{E,B}+V_{O,\widehat d_m}/N_{O,B}\}-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), and
\[
 \frac{\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-(\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0})\}}
 {\widehat s_B}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
Let \(z_{1-\eta/2}\) be the \((1-\eta/2)\)-quantile of the standard normal law and define
\[
 I_B=\left[
 \widehat\tau_B-z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B},
 \widehat\tau_B+z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B}
 \right].
\]
Then \(P\{\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0}\in I_B\}\to1-\eta\). If, in addition, \(\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}=\tau\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\), then the same studentized limit is centered at \(\tau\) and \(P\{\tau\in I_B\}\to1-\eta\).

changed.to:
For a fixed short-term-outcome system, suppose first that the conditions of Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang Theorem 7 hold: Assumptions 1--4 and 6 define the local semiparametric model; at the law under evaluation, Assumptions 6 and 7 admit unique square-integrable outcome and selection bridges; the corresponding conditional-expectation operator \(T_d\) is bijective; and the two source-score second moments \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) are finite. Then their Theorem 7 identifies the two-source gradient as the canonical gradient and gives the local efficiency lower bound
\[
 \sigma_d^2
 =\lim (n_E+n_O)\left(\frac{V_{E,d}}{n_E}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_O}\right)
\]
along any sequence for which the displayed limit exists. For attainment by the doubly robust estimator, additionally impose the sampling and estimation premises of their Theorem 5: independent i.i.d. observations within the two sources, \(n_E,n_O\to\infty\), \(n_E/n_O\) converging to a number in \((0,\infty)\), both identification-and-consistency premises in statements 1 and 2 of their Theorem 4, cross-fitting, and both parts of their Assumption 8 with the nuisance limits equal to the true bridges, all weak- and strong-metric errors vanishing, and the minimum of the outcome-weak--selection-strong and outcome-strong--selection-weak error products equal to \(o((n_E+n_O)^{-1/2})\). Under these additional premises, their Theorem 5 gives asymptotic normality with variance \(\sigma_d^2\), so the estimator attains the Theorem 7 local semiparametric efficiency lower bound. Equivalently, on the original estimator scale, the leading variance is \(V_{E,d}/n_E+V_{O,d}/n_O\).
changed.reason: The current citation claim suppresses premises that differ between the two cited theorems. Theorem 7 supplies the canonical-gradient and efficiency conclusion at a fixed law under unique bridges and bijectivity, whereas attainment by the estimator also requires the sampling-ratio, identification, cross-fitting, nuisance-convergence, product-rate, and moment conditions used by Theorem 5. The replacement gives the precise theorem-to-assumption map and does not infer causal efficiency from bijectivity alone.

\]

\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u
 \bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t+\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4 k_{j,u}(w_j).                                    \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment.  The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant. \]

\[
 0<\delta_\epsilon<\min\{r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{reg}},r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{opt}}\}

For a fixed short-term-outcome system, write \(\tau_0\) for its causal average long-term treatment effect and let \(n=n_E+n_O\).  Use a fixed number \(L_0\ge2\) of observational cross-fitting folds, independent i.i.d. observations within the two mutually independent sources, \(n_E,n_O\to\infty\), and \(n_E/n_O\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\).  Suppose the conditions of Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang Theorem~4 statements 1 and 2 both hold.  Explicitly, the causal and completeness conditions used by their Theorems~1 and 2 hold; their Assumptions~6 and 7 furnish square-integrable latent outcome and selection bridges \(h_0\) and \(q_0\); the corresponding observed conditional-moment equations hold; and both parts of their Assumption~8 hold with nuisance limits equal to \(h_0\) and \(q_0\).  Let \(\mathsf T_0\) and \(\mathsf T_0^\star\) be the conditional-expectation operator and adjoint defined immediately before their Assumption~8.  Thus, for every fold \(1\le\ell\le L_0\),
\[
 \|\mathsf T_0(\widehat h^{(-\ell)}-h_0)\|_2=O_P(\delta_{h,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat h^{(-\ell)}-h_0\|_2=O_P(\rho_{h,n}),
\]
\[
 \|\mathsf T_0^\star(\widehat q^{(-\ell)}-q_0)\|_2=O_P(\delta_{q,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat q^{(-\ell)}-q_0\|_2=O_P(\rho_{q,n}),
\]
where all four deterministic rates tend to zero and
\[
 \min\{\delta_{h,n}\rho_{q,n},\rho_{h,n}\delta_{q,n}\}
 =o(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Write \(V_E\) and \(V_O\) for the experimental and observational source-score second moments displayed in their Theorem~5, and assume
\[
 0<\min\{V_E,V_O\}\le\max\{V_E,V_O\}<\infty.
\]
Then
\[
 \sigma^2=\frac{1+\lambda}{\lambda}V_E+(1+\lambda)V_O
\]
is finite and strictly positive, and their cross-fitted doubly robust estimator satisfies
\[
 \sqrt n\,(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DR}}-\tau_0)
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2).
\]
In particular, the published theorem is centered at the causal target \(\tau_0\) under its two identification premises; it does not assert an observed-bridge-centered limit on a larger model where those premises may fail.

For a fixed short-term-outcome system, write \(\tau_0\) for its causal average long-term treatment effect and let \(n=n_E+n_O\).  Use a fixed number \(L_0\ge2\) of observational cross-fitting folds, independent i.i.d. observations within the two mutually independent sources, \(n_E,n_O\to\infty\), and \(n_E/n_O\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\).  Suppose the conditions of Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang Theorem~4 statements 1 and 2 both hold.  Explicitly, the causal and completeness conditions used by their Theorems~1 and 2 hold; their Assumptions~6 and 7 furnish square-integrable latent outcome and selection bridges \(h_0\) and \(q_0\); the corresponding observed conditional-moment equations hold; and both parts of their Assumption~8 hold with nuisance limits equal to \(h_0\) and \(q_0\).  Let \(\mathsf T_0\) and \(\mathsf T_0^\star\) be the conditional-expectation operator and adjoint defined immediately before their Assumption~8.  Thus, for every fold \(1\le\ell\le L_0\),
\[
 \|\mathsf T_0(\widehat h^{(-\ell)}-h_0)\|_2=O_P(\delta_{h,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat h^{(-\ell)}-h_0\|_2=O_P(\rho_{h,n}),
\]
\[
 \|\mathsf T_0^\star(\widehat q^{(-\ell)}-q_0)\|_2=O_P(\delta_{q,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat q^{(-\ell)}-q_0\|_2=O_P(\rho_{q,n}),
\]
where all four deterministic rates tend to zero and
\[
 \min\{\delta_{h,n}\rho_{q,n},\rho_{h,n}\delta_{q,n}\}
 =o(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Write \(V_E\) and \(V_O\) for the experimental and observational source-score second moments displayed in their Theorem~5, and assume
\[
 0<\min\{V_E,V_O\}\le\max\{V_E,V_O\}<\infty.
\]
Then
\[
 \sigma^2=\frac{1+\lambda}{\lambda}V_E+(1+\lambda)V_O
\]
is finite and strictly positive, and their cross-fitted doubly robust estimator satisfies
\[
 \sqrt n\,(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DR}}-\tau_0)
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2).
\]
In particular, the published theorem is centered at the causal target \(\tau_0\) under its two identification premises; it does not assert an observed-bridge-centered limit on a larger model where those premises may fail.
changed.to:
For a fixed short-term-outcome system and source-conditional law \(P\), let \(n=n_E+n_O\) and define the artificial superpopulation law \(P_n^{\circ}\) by
\[
 P_n^{\circ}(G=E)=\frac{n_E}{n},
 \qquad
 P_n^{\circ}(G=O)=\frac{n_O}{n},
 \qquad
 P_n^{\circ}(\cdot\mid G=g)=P(\cdot\mid G=g).
\]
Every norm in the statement below is \(\|\cdot\|_2=\|\cdot\|_{L_2(P_n^{\circ})}\).  Use a fixed number \(L_0\ge2\) of observational-only cross-fitting folds, independent i.i.d. observations within the two mutually independent sources, \(n_E,n_O\to\infty\), and \(n_E/n_O\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\).  Suppose Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang Theorem~4 statements 1 and 2, their square-integrable latent outcome and selection bridge premises, the corresponding observed moment equations, and both parts of their Assumption~8 hold with nuisance limits equal to the true bridges \(h_0\) and \(q_0\).  Thus, for every \(1\le\ell\le L_0\),
\[
 \|\mathsf T_0(\widehat h^{(-\ell)}-h_0)\|_2=O_P(\delta_{h,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat h^{(-\ell)}-h_0\|_2=O_P(\rho_{h,n}),
\]
\[
 \|\mathsf T_0^\star(\widehat q^{(-\ell)}-q_0)\|_2=O_P(\delta_{q,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat q^{(-\ell)}-q_0\|_2=O_P(\rho_{q,n}),
\]
all four rates tend to zero, and
\[
 \min\{\delta_{h,n}\rho_{q,n},\rho_{h,n}\delta_{q,n}\}
 =o(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Define the two score moments printed in their Theorem~5, kept distinct from this paper's arm-normalized \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\), by
\[
 V_E^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \left\{\frac{A-P(A=1\mid G=E)}{P(A=1\mid G=E)}
 \bigl(h_0(S_3,S_2,A,X)-\mu_0(A)\bigr)\right\}^2
 \mathrel{\Big|}G=E\right]
\]
and
\[
 V_O^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \left\{\frac{A-P(A=1\mid G=O)}{P(A=1\mid G=O)}
 q_0(S_2,S_1,A,X)
 \bigl(Y-h_0(S_3,S_2,A,X)\bigr)\right\}^2
 \mathrel{\Big|}G=O\right].
\]
If these two moments are finite and strictly positive, their Theorem~5 states that
\[
 \sqrt n\,(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DR}}-\tau_0)
 \rightsquigarrow
 \mathcal N\!\left(0,
 \frac{1+\lambda}{\lambda}V_E^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 +(1+\lambda)V_O^{\mathrm{IKM}}\right).
\]
This cited statement records the source's printed normalization only.  It neither identifies \(V_g^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) with this paper's \(V_{g,d}\) nor supplies the arm-normalized fixed-path expansion used by the post-selection theorem.

For a fixed short-term-outcome system, suppose first that the conditions of Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang Theorem 7 hold: Assumptions 1--4 and 6 define the local semiparametric model; at the law under evaluation, Assumptions 6 and 7 admit unique square-integrable outcome and selection bridges; the corresponding conditional-expectation operator \(T_d\) is bijective; and the two source-score second moments \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) are finite. Then their Theorem 7 identifies the two-source gradient as the canonical gradient and gives the local efficiency lower bound
\[
 \sigma_d^2
 =\lim (n_E+n_O)\left(\frac{V_{E,d}}{n_E}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_O}\right)
\]
along any sequence for which the displayed limit exists. For attainment by the doubly robust estimator, additionally impose the sampling and estimation premises of their Theorem 5: independent i.i.d. observations within the two sources, \(n_E,n_O\to\infty\), \(n_E/n_O\) converging to a number in \((0,\infty)\), both identification-and-consistency premises in statements 1 and 2 of their Theorem 4, cross-fitting, and both parts of their Assumption 8 with the nuisance limits equal to the true bridges, all weak- and strong-metric errors vanishing, and the minimum of the outcome-weak--selection-strong and outcome-strong--selection-weak error products equal to \(o((n_E+n_O)^{-1/2})\). Under these additional premises, their Theorem 5 gives asymptotic normality with variance \(\sigma_d^2\), so the estimator attains the Theorem 7 local semiparametric efficiency lower bound. Equivalently, on the original estimator scale, the leading variance is \(V_{E,d}/n_E+V_{O,d}/n_O\).
changed.to:
For a fixed short-term-outcome system and a design \(d\), let \(V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) and \(V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) denote the two source-score second moments printed in Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang Theorem~5 for the causal target \(\tau\). Suppose the conditions of their Theorem~7 hold: their Assumptions~1--4 and~6 define the local semiparametric model; at the law under evaluation, their Assumptions~6 and~7 admit unique square-integrable outcome and selection bridges; the corresponding conditional-expectation operator is bijective; and \(V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) and \(V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) are finite. Then their Theorem~7 identifies the printed two-source gradient as the canonical gradient and gives the local efficiency lower bound
\[
 \sigma_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^2
 =\lim (n_E+n_O)\left(
 \frac{V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}{n_E}
 +\frac{V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}{n_O}
 \right)
\]
along any sequence for which the displayed limit exists. For attainment, additionally impose the sampling and estimation premises of their Theorem~5: independent identically distributed observations within the two sources, \(n_E,n_O\to\infty\), \(n_E/n_O\) converging to a number in \((0,\infty)\), both identification-and-consistency premises in statements~1 and~2 of their Theorem~4, cross-fitting, and both parts of their Assumption~8 with nuisance limits equal to the true bridges, all weak- and strong-metric errors vanishing, and the minimum of the outcome-weak--selection-strong and outcome-strong--selection-weak error products equal to \(o((n_E+n_O)^{-1/2})\). Under these additional premises, their Theorem~5 gives asymptotic normality with variance \(\sigma_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^2\), so their doubly robust estimator attains the Theorem~7 lower bound for \(\tau\). Equivalently, on the original estimator scale, the leading variance is \(V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}/n_E+V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}/n_O\).

More precisely,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},\qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]

The same divergence holds on the relatively open range of cap-feasible cost vectors satisfying
\[
 1<\frac{c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}}
 {c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}}<\frac{48}{35},
\]
for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\). Thus the failure is neither an equal-cost artifact nor an identification failure.

For the unequal-cost binary witness, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives a law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) for which both designs identify \(\tau\) and are regular. Although \(d_{\mathrm p}\) is more expensive, with \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=6>5=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}\), it is the unique minimizer of this paper's Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped paired-source prediction objective, while \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is the unique minimizer of both the paper's arm-normalized profile and the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang-normalized causal efficiency profile. More precisely,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
\]
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). On the relatively open subregion \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\subseteq\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\), every design remains regular and identifies \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)=\infty.
\]
The same center-path divergence, for both ratios, holds on the relatively open range of cap-feasible cost vectors satisfying
\[
 1<\frac{c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}}
 {c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}}<\frac{48}{35},
\]
for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\). Thus the failure is neither an equal-cost artifact nor an identification failure, and the absolute causal-efficiency interpretation uses the IKM-normalized profile rather than the unscaled arm-normalized profile.

Conditional on the independent full-catalogue pilot, suppose that the purchased experimental and observational samples are mutually independent and consist of independent and identically distributed observations from \(P(\cdot\mid G=E)\) and \(P(\cdot\mid G=O)\), respectively.

Use a fixed integer \(L\ge2\) of observational-only cross-fitting folds. For deterministic \(d_B\in\mathcal D\) and \(\alpha_B\in(0,1)\), put
\[
 e_B=\left\lfloor\frac{\alpha_BB}{c_{E,d_B}}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad
 o_B=\left\lfloor\frac{(1-\alpha_B)B}{c_{O,d_B}}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad n_B=e_B+o_B,
\]
and let \(P_{B,d_B,\alpha_B}^{\circ}\) have source probabilities \(e_B/n_B\) and \(o_B/n_B\) and source-conditional laws \(P(\cdot\mid G=E)\) and \(P(\cdot\mid G=O)\). Write \(\|\cdot\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=\|\cdot\|_{L_2(P_{B,d_B,\alpha_B}^{\circ})}\). Along every deterministic sequence satisfying
\[
 |\alpha_B-\alpha_{d_B}^*(P)|\longrightarrow0, \tag{1}
\]
suppose, uniformly over \(1\le\ell\le L\), that with \(\Delta h_{B,\ell}=\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_{d_B}\) and \(\Delta q_{B,\ell}=\widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_{d_B}\),
\[
 \|T_{d_B}\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\delta_{h,B}),
 \qquad
 \|\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\rho_{h,B}), \tag{2}
\]
\[
 \|T_{d_B}^{\star}\Delta q_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\delta_{q,B}),
 \qquad
 \|\Delta q_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\rho_{q,B}), \tag{3}
\]
where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and
\[
 \min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2}). \tag{4}
\]
Suppose also that the foldwise empirical multipliers obey
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \max_{1\le\ell\le L}\bigl(&
 \|\mathbf 1\{G=O\}\Delta q_{B,\ell}(Y-h_{d_B})\|_{2,B}^{\circ}
 +\|\mathbf 1\{G=O\}q_{d_B}\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}\\
 &+\|\mathbf 1\{G=O\}\Delta q_{B,\ell}\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}
 \bigr)=o_P(1),
\end{aligned} \tag{5}

{"id":"thm:postselection-wald","kind":"theorem","statement":"Fix an arbitrary \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) and write \(\theta_d(P)=\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}\). Conditional on the independent full-catalogue pilot, suppose that the purchased experimental and observational samples are mutually independent and consist of independent and identically distributed observations from \(P(\cdot\mid G=E)\) and \(P(\cdot\mid G=O)\), respectively.

Use a fixed integer \(L\ge2\) of observational-only cross-fitting folds. For deterministic \(d_B\in\mathcal D\) and \(\alpha_B\in(0,1)\), put
\[
 e_B=\left\lfloor\frac{\alpha_BB}{c_{E,d_B}}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad
 o_B=\left\lfloor\frac{(1-\alpha_B)B}{c_{O,d_B}}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad n_B=e_B+o_B,
\]
and let \(P_{B,d_B,\alpha_B}^{\circ}\) have source probabilities \(e_B/n_B\) and \(o_B/n_B\) and source-conditional laws \(P(\cdot\mid G=E)\) and \(P(\cdot\mid G=O)\). Write \(\|\cdot\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=\|\cdot\|_{L_2(P_{B,d_B,\alpha_B}^{\circ})}\). Along every deterministic sequence satisfying
\[
 |\alpha_B-\alpha_{d_B}^*(P)|\longrightarrow0, \tag{1}
\]
suppose, uniformly over \(1\le\ell\le L\), that with \(\Delta h_{B,\ell}=\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_{d_B}\) and \(\Delta q_{B,\ell}=\widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_{d_B}\),
\[
 \|T_{d_B}\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\delta_{h,B}),
 \qquad
 \|\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\rho_{h,B}), \tag{2}
\]
\[
 \|T_{d_B}^{\star}\Delta q_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\delta_{q,B}),
 \qquad
 \|\Delta q_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\rho_{q,B}), \tag{3}
\]
where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and
\[
 \min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2}). \tag{4}
\]
Suppose also that the foldwise empirical multipliers obey
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \max_{1\le\ell\le L}\bigl(&
 \|\mathbf 1\{G=O\}\Delta q_{B,\ell}(Y-h_{d_B})\|_{2,B}^{\circ}
 +\|\mathbf 1\{G=O\}q_{d_B}\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}\\
 &+\|\mathbf 1\{G=O\}\Delta q_{B,\ell}\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}
 \bigr)=o_P(1),
\end{aligned} \tag{5}
\]
with every bridge evaluated at its design-specific arguments. For each \(o_B\), partition the observational indices deterministically into balanced folds \(O_{B,1},\ldots,O_{B,L}\). Train \(\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}\) on \(O_B\setminus O_{B,\ell}\) and \(\widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}\) on \(E_B\cup(O_B\setminus O_{B,\ell})\), with any auxiliary training randomness independent of evaluation observations; assign every degenerate fit a fixed measurable value. Evaluate every experimental observation with every one of the \(L\) outcome-bridge fits.

For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), put
\[
 e_{B,a}=\sum_{i\in E_B}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\},
 \qquad
 o_{B,\ell,a}=\sum_{i\in O_{B,\ell}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\},
\]
and, on positive denominators, define
\[
 \widehat p_{E,a}=e_{B,a}/e_B,
 \qquad
 \widehat p_{O,\ell,a}=o_{B,\ell,a}/|O_{B,\ell}|,
\]
\[
 \widehat\mu_{d_B,a}^{(-\ell)}
 =\frac1{e_{B,a}}\sum_{i\in E_B}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}
 \widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d_B,i},S_{2d_B,i},a,X_i),
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\mu_{B,d_B}(a)
 &=\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\widehat\mu_{d_B,a}^{(-\ell)}\\
 &\quad+\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\frac1{o_{B,\ell,a}}
 \sum_{i\in O_{B,\ell}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}
 \widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{2d_B,i},S_{1d_B,i},a,X_i)\\
 &\hspace{36mm}\times
 \{Y_i-\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d_B,i},S_{2d_B,i},a,X_i)\},
\end{aligned} \tag{6}
\]
and \(\widehat\tau_B(d_B,\alpha_B)=\widehat\mu_{B,d_B}(1)-\widehat\mu_{B,d_B}(0)\). Define the exact arm-normalized plug-in scores by
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\phi_{E,d_B,B,i}
 =\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{a=0}^1(-1)^{1-a}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}}{\widehat p_{E,a}}
 \{&\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d_B,i},S_{2d_B,i},a,X_i)
 -\widehat\mu_{d_B,a}^{(-\ell)}\},
\end{aligned} \tag{7}
\]
for \(i\in E_B\), and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\phi_{O,d_B,B,i}
 &=\sum_{a=0}^1(-1)^{1-a}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}}{\widehat p_{O,\ell,a}}
 \widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{2d_B,i},S_{1d_B,i},a,X_i)\\
 &\hspace{22mm}\times
 \{Y_i-\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d_B,i},S_{2d_B,i},a,X_i)\},
 \qquad i\in O_{B,\ell}.
\end{aligned} \tag{8}
\]
Set \(\widetilde V_{E,d_B,B}=e_B^{-1}\sum_{i\in E_B}\widehat\phi_{E,d_B,B,i}^2\) and \(\widetilde V_{O,d_B,B}=o_B^{-1}\sum_{i\in O_B}\widehat\phi_{O,d_B,B,i}^2\). Every quantity in (6)--(8), including the two variance estimators, is assigned zero whenever one of its displayed denominators is zero.

\[

\[

 \cap\bigcap_{a=0}^1\{e_{B,a}\ge1\}\\
 &{}\cap\bigcap_{\ell=1}^L\bigcap_{a=0}^1\{o_{B,\ell,a}\ge1\}.
\end{aligned} \tag{11}
\]
With all zero-denominator fractions assigned zero, set
\[
 \widehat s_B^2
 =\mathbf 1\{\mathsf D_B\}B\left\{
 \frac{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}}{N_{E,B}}
 +\frac{\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}}{N_{O,B}}
 \right\},
 \qquad
 \widehat s_B=(\widehat s_B^2)^{1/2}, \tag{12}
\]
and \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}=\mathsf D_B\cap\{\widehat s_B^2>0\}\). Let \(s_{0,B}\) be the nonnegative square root of
\[
 s_{0,B}^2
 =B\left\{\frac{V_{E,\widehat d_m}}{N_{E,B}}
 +\frac{V_{O,\widehat d_m}}{N_{O,B}}\right\} \tag{13}
\]
when both source counts are positive, and set \(s_{0,B}=0\) otherwise. On \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}\), set \(\widehat\tau_B=\widehat\tau_B(\widehat d_m,\widehat\alpha_m)\), define
\[
 \mathsf T_B=\frac{\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\}}{\widehat s_B},
 \qquad
 I_B=\left[\widehat\tau_B-z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B},
 \widehat\tau_B+z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B}\right], \tag{14}
\]
and on \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}^c\) set \(\widehat\tau_B=0\), \(\widehat s_B=0\), \(\mathsf T_B=0\), and \(I_B=[0,0]\). Then
\[
 P(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}})\longrightarrow1, \tag{15}
\]
\[
 s_{0,B}^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1),
 \qquad
 \widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1), \tag{16}
\]
\[
 \mathsf T_B\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1),
 \qquad
 P\{\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\in I_B\}\longrightarrow1-\eta. \tag{17}
\]
If, in addition, \(\theta_d(P)=\tau\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\), then \(\mathsf T_B\) is the same statistic centered at \(\tau\), \(\sqrt B(\widehat\tau_B-\tau)/\widehat s_B\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\) with the stipulated zero extension, and \(P\{\tau\in I_B\}\to1-\eta\).","free_symbols":["P","\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}","m","B","\mathcal P_m","\mathcal D","d","\alpha","c_{E,d}","c_{O,d}","\alpha_d^*(P)","\mathcal V_d^*(P)","\widehat d_m","\widehat\alpha_{d,m}","\widehat\alpha_m","\underline v_m","\theta_d(P)","\mu_{d,a}","\tau","L","e_B","o_B","n_B","P_{B,d,\alpha}^{\circ}","\|\cdot\|_{2,B}^{\circ}","A","X","Y","S_{1d}","S_{2d}","S_{3d}","T_d","T_d^\star","\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}","h_d","\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}","q_d","\delta_{h,B}","\rho_{h,B}","\delta_{q,B}","\rho_{q,B}","r_{V,m}","r_{\widetilde V,B}","\widehat V_{E,d}","\widehat V_{O,d}","V_{E,d}","V_{O,d}","\widetilde V_{g,d,B}","N_{E,B}","N_{O,B}","e_{B,a}","o_{B,\ell,a}","\widehat p_{E,a}","\widehat p_{O,\ell,a}","\widehat\mu_{d,a}^{(-\ell)}","\widehat\mu_{B,d}(a)","\widehat\tau_B(d,\alpha)","\widehat\phi_{E,d,B,i}","\widehat\phi_{O,d,B,i}","\mathsf D_B","\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}","s_{0,B}","\widehat\tau_B","\widehat s_B^2","\widehat s_B","\mathsf T_B","\eta","z_{1-\eta/2}","I_B"],"depends_on":["lem:designwise-gradient","thm:pilot-oracle-regret","ass:nondegenerate-components","ass:experimental-overlap","ass:observational-overlap","ass:selection-bridge-existence","ass:independent-pilot","ass:uniform-outcome-weak-rate","ass:uniform-outcome-strong-rate","ass:uniform-selection-weak-rate","ass:uniform-selection-strong-rate","ass:outcome-weak-rate-vanishes","ass:outcome-strong-rate-vanishes","ass:selection-weak-rate-vanishes","ass:selection-strong-rate-vanishes","ass:uniform-bridge-product-rate","ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate","ass:pilot-variance-rate-vanishes","ass:main-gradient-variance-rate","ass:main-variance-rate-vanishes","def:pilot-selector","def:selected-wald-variance"],"status":"to-prove"}

{"id":"def:selected-wald-variance","name":"Selected-design Wald estimator and total variance","construction":"Let \(\mathcal I_{E,B}\) and \(\mathcal I_{O,B}\) be the experimental and observational main-study index sets, of sizes \(N_{E,B}\) and \(N_{O,B}\). Use a fixed integer \(L\ge2\) and a deterministic balanced observational-only partition \(\mathcal I_{O,B}=\bigsqcup_{\ell=1}^L\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}\). For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), train \(\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}\) on \(\mathcal I_{O,B}\setminus\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}\), and train \(\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}\) on \(\mathcal I_{E,B}\cup(\mathcal I_{O,B}\setminus\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell})\). Assign any degenerate fit a fixed measurable value.

For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
 e_{B,a}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{E,B}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\},
 \qquad
 o_{B,\ell,a}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\},
\]
\[
 \widehat p_{E,a}=e_{B,a}/N_{E,B},
 \qquad
 \widehat p_{O,\ell,a}=o_{B,\ell,a}/|\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}|,
\]
and
\[
 \widehat\mu_{d,a}^{(-\ell)}
 =\frac1{e_{B,a}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{E,B}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}
 \widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d,i},S_{2d,i},a,X_i).
\]
Every displayed quantity is assigned zero if one of its displayed denominators is zero. Whenever the required denominators are positive, set
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\mu_{B,d}(a)
 &=\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\widehat\mu_{d,a}^{(-\ell)}\\
 &\quad+\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\frac1{o_{B,\ell,a}}
 \sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}
 \widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{2d,i},S_{1d,i},a,X_i)\\
 &\hspace{35mm}\times
 \{Y_i-\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d,i},S_{2d,i},a,X_i)\},
\end{aligned}
\]
and \(\widehat\tau_B(d,\alpha)=\widehat\mu_{B,d}(1)-\widehat\mu_{B,d}(0)\). For \(i\in\mathcal I_{E,B}\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\phi_{E,d,B,i}
 =\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{a=0}^1(-1)^{1-a}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}}{\widehat p_{E,a}}
 \{&\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d,i},S_{2d,i},a,X_i)
 -\widehat\mu_{d,a}^{(-\ell)}\},
\end{aligned}
\]
and, for \(i\in\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\phi_{O,d,B,i}
 &=\sum_{a=0}^1(-1)^{1-a}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}}{\widehat p_{O,\ell,a}}
 \widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{2d,i},S_{1d,i},a,X_i)\\
 &\hspace{22mm}\times
 \{Y_i-\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d,i},S_{2d,i},a,X_i)\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every summand with a zero empirical arm probability is zero. Set
\[
 \widetilde V_{E,d,B}=N_{E,B}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{E,B}}\widehat\phi_{E,d,B,i}^2,
 \qquad
 \widetilde V_{O,d,B}=N_{O,B}^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}}\widehat\phi_{O,d,B,i}^2,
\]
with value zero when the corresponding source count is zero. At \((d,\alpha)=(\widehat d_m,\widehat\alpha_m)\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathsf D_B
 ={}&\{N_{E,B}\ge1,N_{O,B}\ge1\}
 \cap\bigcap_{a=0}^1\{e_{B,a}\ge1\}\\
 &{}\cap\bigcap_{\ell=1}^L\bigcap_{a=0}^1\{o_{B,\ell,a}\ge1\},
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
 \widehat s_B^2=\mathbf 1\{\mathsf D_B\}B\left\{
 \frac{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}}{N_{E,B}}
 +\frac{\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}}{N_{O,B}}\right\},
 \qquad
 \widehat s_B=(\widehat s_B^2)^{1/2},
\]
and \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}=\mathsf D_B\cap\{\widehat s_B^2>0\}\). Let \(s_{0,B}\) be the nonnegative square root of \(B\{V_{E,\widehat d_m}/N_{E,B}+V_{O,\widehat d_m}/N_{O,B}\}\) on positive source counts and zero otherwise. On \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}\), set \(\widehat\tau_B=\widehat\tau_B(\widehat d_m,\widehat\alpha_m)\), \(\mathsf T_B=\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\}/\widehat s_B\), and
\[
 I_B=\left[\widehat\tau_B-z_{1-\eta/2}\widehat s_B/\sqrt B,
 \widehat\tau_B+z_{1-\eta/2}\widehat s_B/\sqrt B\right].
\]
On \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}^c\), set \(\widehat\tau_B=0\), \(\widehat s_B=0\), \(\mathsf T_B=0\), and \(I_B=[0,0]\). Under common identification, \(\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)=\tau\), so the numerator of \(\mathsf T_B\) is equivalently \(\sqrt B(\widehat\tau_B-\tau)\). These conventions make every estimator, score moment, statistic, and interval a fixed measurable map on the entire sample space.","free_symbols":["\mathcal I_{E,B}","\mathcal I_{O,B}","\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}","N_{E,B}","N_{O,B}","L","d","\mathcal D","a","A","X","Y","S_{1d}","S_{2d}","S_{3d}","\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}","\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}","e_{B,a}","o_{B,\ell,a}","\widehat p_{E,a}","\widehat p_{O,\ell,a}","\widehat\mu_{d,a}^{(-\ell)}","\widehat\mu_{B,d}(a)","\widehat\tau_B(d,\alpha)","\widehat\phi_{E,d,B,i}","\widehat\phi_{O,d,B,i}","\widetilde V_{g,d,B}","\widehat d_m","\widehat\alpha_m","\mathsf D_B","\widehat s_B^2","\widehat s_B","\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}","s_{0,B}","\mathsf T_B","\theta_d(P)","P","\eta","z_{1-\eta/2}","I_B","\tau","B"],"inputs":["def:pilot-selector"]}

{"id":"def:binary-region","name":"Relatively open binary perturbation region","construction":"Fix the catalogue, costs, cap, and the two role assignments exactly as in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\).  Name as the \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} the family \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}\) of laws \(P\) with constant \(X\) and constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
 Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u
 \bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t+\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4 k_{j,u}(w_j).                                    \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment.  The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant.  The witness \(P_\epsilon\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
 k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
 \qquad (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,3/4,1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices.  Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (1).  For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), let \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{reg}}>0\) be furnished by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}regular\text{-}locus\text{-}relatively\text{-}open}\), and let \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{opt}}>0\) be the optimizer-stability radius furnished by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\).  Choose
\[
 0<\delta_\epsilon<\min\{r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{reg}},r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{opt}}\}
\]
and define
\[
 \mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}
 =\bigcup_{0<\epsilon<10^{-3}}
 \left\{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}:
 \|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<\delta_\epsilon\right\}.     \tag{2}
\]
Thus each set in the union is a relative open ball in the named model, and \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is relatively open there.  The regular-neighborhood lemma proves, rather than defines, that \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\).  No claim of openness in the ambient unrestricted probability simplex is made, because the factorization, support, consistency, and causal equality restrictions define a lower-dimensional model.","free_symbols":["P","P_{\epsilon}","\epsilon","\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}","\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}","\mathcal D","X","S_{2d}","G","g","U","T","A","Z(a)","Y(a)","a","d_{\mathrm p}","d_{\mathrm e}"],"inputs":["def:binary-witness","def:regular-law-class","lem:binary-regular-locus-relatively-open","lem:binary-witness-stability"]}

More precisely,
\[
V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},
\qquad V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
\qquad V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
\]
\[
\mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)=\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon),
\qquad
\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)=\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). On the relatively open subregion \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\subseteq\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\), every design remains regular and identifies \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)=\infty.
\]
The same center-path divergence, for both ratios, holds for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\) on the relatively open subset of the induced cap-feasible catalogue-cost manifold
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal C_\kappa=\biggl\{(b_E,b_O,c_1,\ldots,c_K):{}&0<b_E<b_O,\quad c_j>0,\\
&\sum_{j\in M_d}c_j\le\kappa\quad(d\in\mathcal D),\\
&c_{E,d}=b_E+\sum_{j\in M_d}c_j,\quad
c_{O,d}=b_O+\sum_{j\in M_d}c_j\quad(d\in\mathcal D)\biggr\}
\end{aligned}
\]
on which
\[
1<\frac{c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}}{c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}}<\frac{48}{35}.
\]

 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_\epsilon;B)

{"id":"def:binary-witness","name":"Binary two-design arbitrary-cost-disadvantage witness family","construction":"Fix an arbitrary prescribed \(\chi>1\). Set \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=(5\chi-3)/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=(5\chi-3)/2\), and put
\[
 y_{\chi}=\sqrt{1-\frac{3}{10\chi}}.
\]
Let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form
\[
 Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}),
\]
while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{y_{\chi}}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi-1}{2},\qquad
 c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi+1}{2},\qquad
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2,\qquad c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3,
\]
so the paired costs are \(5\chi\) and \(5\), respectively. For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are
\[
 h_d(l,a)=\frac{l}{y},
 \qquad
 q_d(e,a)=\frac{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)}{1-1/16},
\]
and the residual prediction variance is
\[
 R(x,y)=\frac{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}{1-x^2y^2}.
\]

The \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) is the family of laws \(P\) with the preceding prescribed catalogue, costs, cap, and role assignments, constant \(X\) and constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
 Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u\bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t
 +\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}

For a fixed short-term-outcome system and a design \(d\), let \(V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) and \(V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) denote the two source-score second moments printed in Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang Theorem~5 for the causal target \(\tau\). Suppose the conditions of their Theorem~7 hold: their Assumptions~1--4 and~6 define the local semiparametric model; at the law under evaluation, their Assumptions~6 and~7 admit unique square-integrable outcome and selection bridges; the corresponding conditional-expectation operator is bijective; and \(V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) and \(V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) are finite. Then their Theorem~7 identifies the printed two-source gradient as the canonical gradient and gives the local efficiency lower bound
\[
 \sigma_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^2
 =\lim (n_E+n_O)\left(
 \frac{V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}{n_E}
 +\frac{V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}{n_O}
 \right)
\]
along any sequence for which the displayed limit exists. For attainment, additionally impose the sampling and estimation premises of their Theorem~5: independent identically distributed observations within the two sources, \(n_E,n_O\to\infty\), \(n_E/n_O\) converging to a number in \((0,\infty)\), both identification-and-consistency premises in statements~1 and~2 of their Theorem~4, cross-fitting, and both parts of their Assumption~8 with nuisance limits equal to the true bridges, all weak- and strong-metric errors vanishing, and the minimum of the outcome-weak--selection-strong and outcome-strong--selection-weak error products equal to \(o((n_E+n_O)^{-1/2})\). Under these additional premises, their Theorem~5 gives asymptotic normality with variance \(\sigma_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^2\), so their doubly robust estimator attains the Theorem~7 lower bound for \(\tau\). Equivalently, on the original estimator scale, the leading variance is \(V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}/n_E+V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}/n_O\).

The proposed text therefore narrows the asymptotic regime and corrects the attribution without changing the attainment claim.

\[

\]

\[

and \(\widehat\tau_B(d_B,\alpha_B)=\widehat\mu_{B,d_B}(1)-\widehat\mu_{B,d_B}(0)\). Define the exact arm-normalized plug-in scores by
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\phi_{E,d_B,B,i}
 =\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{a=0}^1(-1)^{1-a}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}}{\widehat p_{E,a}}
 \{&\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d_B,i},S_{2d_B,i},a,X_i)
 -\widehat\mu_{d_B,a}^{(-\ell)}\},
\end{aligned} \tag{7}
\]
for \(i\in E_B\), and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\phi_{O,d_B,B,i}
 &=\sum_{a=0}^1(-1)^{1-a}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}}{\widehat p_{O,\ell,a}}
 \widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{2d_B,i},S_{1d_B,i},a,X_i)\\
 &\hspace{22mm}\times
 \{Y_i-\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d_B,i},S_{2d_B,i},a,X_i)\},
 \qquad i\in O_{B,\ell}.
\end{aligned} \tag{8}
\]

Let \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\), assume \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), and assume that \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main study. Suppose
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,
 |\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m}),
 \qquad r_{V,m}=o(1), \tag{9}
\]
and
\[

 \qquad r_{\widetilde V,B}=o(1). \tag{10}
\]

\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathsf D_B
 ={}&\{N_{E,B}\ge1,N_{O,B}\ge1\}
 \cap\bigcap_{a=0}^1\{e_{B,a}\ge1\}\\
 &{}\cap\bigcap_{\ell=1}^L\bigcap_{a=0}^1\{o_{B,\ell,a}\ge1\}.
\end{aligned} \tag{11}
\]
With all zero-denominator fractions assigned zero, set
\[
 \widehat s_B^2
 =\mathbf 1\{\mathsf D_B\}B\left\{
 \frac{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}}{N_{E,B}}
 +\frac{\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}}{N_{O,B}}
 \right\},
 \qquad

\]
and \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}=\mathsf D_B\cap\{\widehat s_B^2>0\}\). Let \(s_{0,B}\) be the nonnegative square root of
\[
 s_{0,B}^2
 =B\left\{\frac{V_{E,\widehat d_m}}{N_{E,B}}
 +\frac{V_{O,\widehat d_m}}{N_{O,B}}\right\} \tag{13}
\]
when both source counts are positive, and set \(s_{0,B}=0\) otherwise. On \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}\), set \(\widehat\tau_B=\widehat\tau_B(\widehat d_m,\widehat\alpha_m)\), define
\[

 \qquad

\[

\[

 \qquad
 \widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1), \tag{16}

\[

 \qquad

For every prescribed finite cost-disadvantage factor \(\chi>1\), the generalized unequal-cost binary witness has paired costs \(5\chi\) for \(d_{\mathrm p}\) and \(5\) for \(d_{\mathrm e}\). For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the center law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) is regular for both designs and both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau=0\). Nevertheless, \(d_{\mathrm p}\) is the unique minimizer of the cost-aware prediction objective, while \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is the unique minimizer of both the arm-normalized profile and the IKM-normalized local causal-efficiency profile. More precisely,
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_\epsilon;B)
 =\frac32\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2y_\chi^2}
 <\frac32<3
 =B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_\epsilon;B),
\]
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}+O_\chi(1),
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
\]
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +O_\chi(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Across the center family, let \(\chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)\) be any cost-disadvantage factor minimizing the exact ratio for sufficiently small \(\epsilon\). Then
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim \frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}\epsilon^{-2/3},
\]
and the least-divergent sharp elbow is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=\epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty.
\]
On the relatively open subregion \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\subseteq\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\), every design remains regular and identifies \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)=\infty.
\]
For each prescribed \(\chi>1\), the center cost vector belongs to \(\mathcal C_\kappa\), has paired-cost ratio exactly \(\chi\), and has a relatively open neighborhood in \(\mathcal C_\kappa\) on which \(d_{\mathrm p}\) remains strictly more expensive and uniquely prediction-selected for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\), while both the arm-normalized and balanced-center IKM-normalized ratios diverge along the center-law path. Thus predictive selection has no finite uniform efficiency guarantee even when its chosen design is required to bear any prescribed finite cost disadvantage; even the least-divergent cost-disadvantage sequence grows at order \(\epsilon^{-2/3}\), and its efficiency ratio retains the leading divergence \(1/(726\epsilon^2)\). The failure is neither an equal-cost artifact nor an identification failure. Absolute causal-efficiency claims use the IKM-normalized profile and the fixed-system premises, whereas the arm-normalized profile is a bridge-gradient design value on the full regular class.

Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) and \(B>0\), and abbreviate
\[
 p_d=\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B),
 \qquad
 v_d=\mathcal V_d^*(P).
\]
Define the prediction-order relation and its order-restricted efficiency constant by
\[
 \mathcal O_P
 =\{(d,d')\in\mathcal D^2:p_d\le p_{d'}\},
 \qquad
 C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)
 =\max_{(d,d')\in\mathcal O_P}\frac{v_d}{v_{d'}}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Then \(1\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\), and, for every \(C\ge0\),
\[
 \bigl[p_d\le p_{d'}\Longrightarrow v_d\le C v_{d'}
 \text{ for all }d,d'\in\mathcal D\bigr]
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 C\ge C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P).
 \tag{2}
\]
The smallest constant for the actual best-tie predictive rule is instead
\[
 C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}v_d}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}v_{d'}}
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P),
 \qquad
 1\le C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty.
 \tag{3}
\]
Consequently, for any nonempty subclass \(\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), a finite constant uniform over \(\mathcal Q\) exists for the best-tie rule if and only if
\(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)<\infty\); for all pairwise prediction-order implications it exists if and only if
\(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\).  Thus (1), rather than an operator norm, is the weakest exact law-primitive comparison for the stated selection problem.  The design-specific operators \(T_d\) enter (1) through the bridges and hence through \(v_d\), but no further comparison of the operators is necessary for lawwise finiteness.

More specifically, consider any numerical realization of the handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\) with the following properties. \[
 Bp_d=Q_{R,d}\{x_d(P)\},
 \qquad
 v_d=F_d\{x_d(P)\},
 \tag{4}
\]
where
\[
 F_d(x)
 =\left\{
 \sqrt{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}
 +\sqrt{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}
 \right\}^2.
 \tag{5}
\]
Set
\[
 \Lambda_-(P)
 =\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\inf_{x\in\mathcal X_d(P)}
 \frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}(x)},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_+(P)
 =\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_d(P)}
 \frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}(x)}.
 \tag{6}
\]
The weakest two-sided quadratic-form envelope on the chosen cones is precisely
\[
 0<\Lambda_-(P)\le\Lambda_+(P)<\infty,
 \tag{7}
\]
and it implies the valid, generally conservative certificate
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 \le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)
 \le\frac{\Lambda_+(P)}{\Lambda_-(P)}.
 \tag{8}
\]

The sharp constant in (2) or (3) is not, in general, a largest generalized eigenvalue.  Indeed,
\[
 F_d(x)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}
 \left\{
 \frac{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}{\alpha}
 +\frac{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}{1-\alpha}
 \right\},
 \tag{9}
\]
so the profiled numerator is generally not a quadratic form. \[

 \qquad

\]
\[

\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +\frac{896}{75(10\chi-3)},

\]
and, as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) with \(\chi\) fixed,

 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}

{"id":"thm:sharp-predictive-operator-certificate","kind":"theorem","statement":"Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) and \(B>0\), and abbreviate
\[
 p_d=\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B),
 \qquad
 v_d=\mathcal V_d^*(P).
\]
Define the prediction-order relation and its order-restricted efficiency constant by
\[
 \mathcal O_P
 =\{(d,d')\in\mathcal D^2:p_d\le p_{d'}\},
 \qquad
 C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)
 =\max_{(d,d')\in\mathcal O_P}\frac{v_d}{v_{d'}}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Then \(1\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\), and, for every \(C\ge0\),
\[
 \bigl[p_d\le p_{d'}\Longrightarrow v_d\le C v_{d'}
 \text{ for all }d,d'\in\mathcal D\bigr]
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 C\ge C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P).
 \tag{2}
\]
The smallest constant for the actual best-tie paired-source diagnostic rule is instead
\[
 C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}v_d}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}v_{d'}}
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P),
 \qquad
 1\le C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty.
 \tag{3}
\]
Consequently, for any nonempty subclass \(\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), a finite constant uniform over \(\mathcal Q\) exists for the best-tie rule if and only if
\(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)<\infty\); for all pairwise prediction-order implications it exists if and only if
\(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\).  Thus (1), rather than an operator norm, is the weakest exact lawwise comparison for selection by this newly defined diagnostic.  The design-specific operators \(T_d\) enter (1) through the bridges and hence through \(v_d\), but no further comparison of the operators is necessary for lawwise finiteness.

 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}).

changed.from:
{"id":"def:selected-wald-variance","name":"Selected-design Wald estimator and total variance","construction":"Let \(\mathcal I_{E,B}\) and \(\mathcal I_{O,B}\) be the experimental and observational main-study index sets, of sizes \(N_{E,B}\) and \(N_{O,B}\). Use a fixed integer \(L\ge2\) and a deterministic balanced observational-only partition \(\mathcal I_{O,B}=\bigsqcup_{\ell=1}^L\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}\). For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), train \(\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}\) on \(\mathcal I_{O,B}\setminus\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}\), and train \(\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}\) on \(\mathcal I_{E,B}\cup(\mathcal I_{O,B}\setminus\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell})\). Assign any degenerate fit a fixed measurable value.

For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
 e_{B,a}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{E,B}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\},
 \qquad
 o_{B,\ell,a}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\},
\]
\[
 \widehat p_{E,a}=e_{B,a}/N_{E,B},
 \qquad
 \widehat p_{O,\ell,a}=o_{B,\ell,a}/|\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}|,
\]
and
\[
 \widehat\mu_{d,a}^{(-\ell)}
 =\frac1{e_{B,a}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{E,B}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}
 \widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d,i},S_{2d,i},a,X_i).
\]
Every displayed quantity is assigned zero if one of its displayed denominators is zero. Whenever the required denominators are positive, set
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\mu_{B,d}(a)
 &=\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\widehat\mu_{d,a}^{(-\ell)}\\
 &\quad+\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\frac1{o_{B,\ell,a}}
 \sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}
 \widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{2d,i},S_{1d,i},a,X_i)\\
 &\hspace{35mm}\times
 \{Y_i-\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d,i},S_{2d,i},a,X_i)\},
\end{aligned}
\]
and \(\widehat\tau_B(d,\alpha)=\widehat\mu_{B,d}(1)-\widehat\mu_{B,d}(0)\). For \(i\in\mathcal I_{E,B}\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\phi_{E,d,B,i}
 =\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{a=0}^1(-1)^{1-a}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}}{\widehat p_{E,a}}
 \{&\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d,i},S_{2d,i},a,X_i)
 -\widehat\mu_{d,a}^{(-\ell)}\},
\end{aligned}
\]
and, for \(i\in\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}

For every prescribed finite cost-disadvantage factor \(\chi>1\), the generalized unequal-cost binary witness has paired costs \(5\chi\) for \(d_{\mathrm p}\) and \(5\) for \(d_{\mathrm e}\). For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the center law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) is regular for both designs and both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau=0\). Nevertheless, \(d_{\mathrm p}\) is the unique minimizer of the new paired-source residual-risk diagnostic, while \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is the unique minimizer of both the arm-normalized profile and the IKM-normalized local causal-efficiency profile. More precisely,
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_\epsilon;B)
 =\frac32\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2y_\chi^2}
 <\frac32<3
 =B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_\epsilon;B),
\]
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}+O_\chi(1),
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
\]
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +O_\chi(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Across the center family, let \(\chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)\) be any cost-disadvantage factor minimizing the exact ratio for sufficiently small \(\epsilon\). Then
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim \frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}\epsilon^{-2/3},
\]
and the least-divergent sharp elbow is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=\epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[

On the relatively open subregion \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\subseteq\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\), every design remains regular and identifies \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)=\infty.
\]
For each prescribed \(\chi>1\), the center cost vector belongs to \(\mathcal C_\kappa\), has paired-cost ratio exactly \(\chi\), and has a relatively open neighborhood in \(\mathcal C_\kappa\) on which \(d_{\mathrm p}\) remains strictly more expensive and uniquely diagnostic-selected for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\), while both the arm-normalized and balanced-center IKM-normalized ratios diverge along the center-law path. Thus selection by the paired-source residual-risk diagnostic has no finite uniform efficiency guarantee even when its chosen design is required to bear any prescribed finite cost disadvantage; even the least-divergent cost-disadvantage sequence grows at order \(\epsilon^{-2/3}\), and its efficiency ratio retains the leading divergence \(1/(726\epsilon^2)\). This diagnostic failure is neither an equal-cost artifact nor an identification failure, and it is not asserted for a named published proxy-selection workflow. Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) and \(B>0\), and abbreviate
\[
 p_d=\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B),
 \qquad
 v_d=\mathcal V_d^*(P).
\]
Define the prediction-order relation and its order-restricted efficiency constant by
\[
 \mathcal O_P
 =\{(d,d')\in\mathcal D^2:p_d\le p_{d'}\},
 \qquad
 C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)
 =\max_{(d,d')\in\mathcal O_P}\frac{v_d}{v_{d'}}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Then \(1\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\), and, for every \(C\ge0\),
\[
 \bigl[p_d\le p_{d'}\Longrightarrow v_d\le C v_{d'}
 \text{ for all }d,d'\in\mathcal D\bigr]
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 C\ge C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P).
 \tag{2}
\]
The smallest constant for the actual best-tie paired-source diagnostic rule is instead
\[
 C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}v_d}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}v_{d'}}
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P),
 \qquad
 1\le C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty.
 \tag{3}
\]
Consequently, for any nonempty subclass \(\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), a finite constant uniform over \(\mathcal Q\) exists for the best-tie rule if and only if
\(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)<\infty\); for all pairwise prediction-order implications it exists if and only if
\(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\).  Thus (1), rather than an operator norm, is the weakest exact lawwise comparison for selection by this newly defined diagnostic.  The design-specific operators \(T_d\) enter (1) through the bridges and hence through \(v_d\), but no further comparison of the operators is necessary for lawwise finiteness.

More specifically, consider any numerical realization of the handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\) with the following properties.  For each \(d\), it supplies a real vector space \(\mathcal H_d\), a cone \(\mathcal X_d(P)\subseteq\mathcal H_d\setminus\{0\}\) containing a transported law-specific direction \(x_d(P)\), a positive prediction quadratic form \(Q_{R,d}\) on that cone, and two nonnegative source-gradient quadratic forms \(Q_{E,d}\) and \(Q_{O,d}\), with
\[
 Bp_d=Q_{R,d}\{x_d(P)\},
 \qquad
 v_d=F_d\{x_d(P)\},
 \tag{4}
\]
where
\[
 F_d(x)
 =\left\{
 \sqrt{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}
 +\sqrt{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}
 \right\}^2.
 \tag{5}
\]
Set
\[
 \Lambda_-(P)
 =\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\inf_{x\in\mathcal X_d(P)}
 \frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}(x)},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_+(P)
 =\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_d(P)}
 \frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}(x)}.
 \tag{6}
\]
The weakest two-sided quadratic-form envelope on the chosen cones is precisely
\[
 0<\Lambda_-(P)\le\Lambda_+(P)<\infty,
 \tag{7}
\]
and it implies the valid, generally conservative certificate
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 \le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)
 \le\frac{\Lambda_+(P)}{\Lambda_-(P)}.
 \tag{8}
\]

The sharp constant in (2) or (3) is not, in general, a largest generalized eigenvalue.  Indeed,
\[
 F_d(x)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}
 \left\{
 \frac{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}{\alpha}
 +\frac{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}{1-\alpha}
 \right\},
 \tag{9}
\]
so the profiled numerator is generally not a quadratic form.  If \(\mathcal H_d\) is finite dimensional, \(Q_{R,d}\) is positive definite, and \(\mathcal X_d(P)=\mathcal H_d\setminus\{0\}\), a largest generalized eigenvalue at a fixed \(\alpha\) gives only a one-sided full-space envelope.  Selection requires both the upper and lower envelopes in (6), and equality in (8) additionally requires saturation by law-realized, diagnostic-ordered directions.  Hence equality with a largest generalized eigenvalue can hold only after adding a common-space representation, a normalization of the positive lower envelope, and the required saturation; none follows from the lawwise operator bijectivity or from the diagnostic ordering alone.

Fix \(\chi>1\) and \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), and write \(P_{\chi,\epsilon}=P_\epsilon\) for the binary center in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\), with the dependence on \(\chi\) made explicit. \[
 R_{d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\frac{3}{10\chi}\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2(1-3/(10\chi))}
 <\frac{3}{10\chi}<\frac3{10}<\frac35
 =R_{d_{\mathrm e}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon}).
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\) and \(D^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\). The raw-risk-selected design is costlier in each source:
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}-c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}
 =c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}-c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}
 =\frac{5(\chi-1)}2>0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 V_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{40\chi}{10\chi-3},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}\left(\epsilon^{-2}+14\right),
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\frac{3872}{25},
\]
and the exact center ratio is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac{25}{3872}
 \left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{20\chi(5\chi-1)}{10\chi-3}}
 +\sqrt{\frac{32(5\chi+1)}{75(10\chi-3)}
 \left(\epsilon^{-2}+14\right)}
 \right\}^{2}.                                             \tag{1}
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 \ge
 \frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}
 \left(\epsilon^{-2}+14\right)
 >\frac{\epsilon^{-2}+14}{726},                            \tag{2}
\]
with the identical inequalities for \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\), and
\[
 \inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 >\frac{\epsilon^{-2}+14}{726}.                            \tag{3}
\]
For all sufficiently small \(\epsilon\), the infimum in (3) is attained. If \(\chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)\) is any minimizer and
\[
 k_\star=\frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15},
\]
then
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim k_\star\epsilon^{-2/3}.                              \tag{4}
\]

\[
 q(k)=2\sqrt{\frac{32k}{15}}+\frac{8}{75k},                \tag{5}
\]
and \(q\) has the unique minimizer \(k_\star\). The sharp second-order uniform elbow is
\[
\begin{aligned}

 &=\epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\

Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(B>0\), and abbreviate
\[
 p_d=\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B),
 \qquad
 v_d=\mathcal V_d^*(P).
\]
Define the prediction-order relation and its order-restricted design-value constant by
\[
 \mathcal O_P
 =\{(d,d')\in\mathcal D^2:p_d\le p_{d'}\},
 \qquad
 C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)
 =\max_{(d,d')\in\mathcal O_P}\frac{v_d}{v_{d'}}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Then \(1\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\), and, for every \(C\ge0\),
\[
 \bigl[p_d\le p_{d'}\Longrightarrow v_d\le C v_{d'}
 \text{ for all }d,d'\in\mathcal D\bigr]
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 C\ge C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P).
 \tag{2}
\]
The smallest constant for the actual best-tie paired-source diagnostic rule is instead
\[
 C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}v_d}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}v_{d'}}
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P),
 \qquad
 1\le C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty.
 \tag{3}
\]
Consequently, for any nonempty subclass \(\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), a finite constant uniform over \(\mathcal Q\) exists for the best-tie rule if and only if
\(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)<\infty\); for all pairwise prediction-order implications it exists if and only if
\(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\).  Thus (1), rather than an operator norm, is the weakest exact lawwise comparison for selection by this newly defined diagnostic.  The design-specific operators \(T_d\) enter (1) through the bridges and hence through \(v_d\), but no further comparison of the operators is necessary for lawwise finiteness.

More specifically, consider any numerical realization of the handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\) with the following properties.  For each \(d\), it supplies a real vector space \(\mathcal H_d\), a cone \(\mathcal X_d(P)\subseteq\mathcal H_d\setminus\{0\}\) containing a transported law-specific direction \(x_d(P)\), a positive prediction quadratic form \(Q_{R,d}\) on that cone, and two nonnegative source-score quadratic forms \(Q_{E,d}\) and \(Q_{O,d}\), with
\[
 Bp_d=Q_{R,d}\{x_d(P)\},
 \qquad
 v_d=F_d\{x_d(P)\},
 \tag{4}
\]
where
\[
 F_d(x)
 =\left\{
 \sqrt{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}
 +\sqrt{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}
 \right\}^2.
 \tag{5}
\]
On the bridge-differentiable submodel class of Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}bridge\text{-}differentiable\text{-}submodel}\), these source scores are gradient components; outside that class, only the source-score interpretation is asserted.  Set
\[
 \Lambda_-(P)
 =\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\inf_{x\in\mathcal X_d(P)}
 \frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}(x)},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_+(P)
 =\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_d(P)}
 \frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}(x)}.
 \tag{6}
\]
The weakest two-sided quadratic-form envelope on the chosen cones is precisely
\[
 0<\Lambda_-(P)\le\Lambda_+(P)<\infty,
 \tag{7}
\]
and it implies the valid, generally conservative certificate
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 \le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)
 \le\frac{\Lambda_+(P)}{\Lambda_-(P)}.
 \tag{8}
\]

The sharp constant in (2) or (3) is not, in general, a largest generalized eigenvalue.  Indeed,
\[
 F_d(x)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}
 \left\{
 \frac{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}{\alpha}
 +\frac{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}{1-\alpha}
 \right\},
 \tag{9}
\]
so the profiled numerator is generally not a quadratic form.  If \(\mathcal H_d\) is finite dimensional, \(Q_{R,d}\) is positive definite, and \(\mathcal X_d(P)=\mathcal H_d\setminus\{0\}\), a largest generalized eigenvalue at a fixed \(\alpha\) gives only a one-sided full-space envelope.  Selection requires both the upper and lower envelopes in (6), and equality in (8) additionally requires saturation by law-realized, diagnostic-ordered directions.  Hence equality with a largest generalized eigenvalue can hold only after adding a common-space representation, a normalization of the positive lower envelope, and the required saturation; none follows from observable-law operator bijectivity or from the diagnostic ordering alone.
